High bur 'ash' / Mid bur 'hole' / High kïc 'stomach' / Mid-Low kïc 'orphan' / High man 'this, these' / High-Low man 'that, who, which'. [p.48 fn.3:] In tone elicitation of initial data, these two sets of pronouns were found to have the same tone (High on attached pronouns and Low on separate pronouns). [p.66 fn.5:] ... new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Re-opened the mirror copy (4,076,188 B, the PDF's metadata 242 pages, created 2015-09-24 from Word). Title page (p.1) reads 'Belanda Bor Grammar Book / Authors: John Baptist Asan, Elias Khamis Kpoyo, Hon. Zitta Sabino Gume, Batista Ucin Utengo, Philip Thomas Singo, Anthony Ngangi Mara, Anas Mahbus Mbolo, Willaim Vaikando Tibur, John Gorgori Rabi, Lino Taban / Trial Edition / SIL-South Sudan'; p.2 '(c) 2015, Belanda Bor Translation and Literacy Project and SIL South Sudan / Trial Edition 2015 / Publisher: SIL-South Sudan / Place of Publication: Juba' = same work as the citation (authors, title, year, publisher, place, 242 pp.). Provenance re-verified: HEADhttps://www.webonary.org/belandabor/…
new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (bela1256 has no catalog record and no stress statement held by the project). What this source adds is tone-only: contrastive H/M/L lexical and grammatical tone, no statement on stress; consistent with the notes already held by the project from PHOIBLE/Gilley 2004 ('three level tones') and Wikipedia<-von Heyking 2013 (tone present but functionally reduced). It neither places stress nor denies it.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The book treats Belanda Bor as a tone language: words contrast by High, Mid and Low tone (and contours High-Low, Mid-Low), with lexical and grammatical minimal pairs (wara/wàrà, ka plural vs kà 'wound', ni 'your' vs ni 'be'); tone is written only on a-vowel minimal pairs (á High, à Low). It defers all sound-system matters to the companion Belanda Bor Consonant and Vowel Book and says nothing about word stress, accent placement or prominence. No stress rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: none on stress. On tone: nine tone patterns on disyllables are referred to the Consonant and Vowel Book; fn.5 p.66 says vowel length is not distinctive (re/ree) pending a tone check, although the 'Vowel rule' p.6 writes most verbs with a long first vowel vs nouns short.
new_statements.identity_note: The SIL primers describe Belanda Bor as written by the Belanda Bor Translation and Literacy Project (Wau area, Western Bahr el Ghazal, South Sudan), orthography workshops led by Tim Stirtz, drawing on von Heyking 2013 (A Grammar of Belanda Boor); no dialect differentiation is made. Not to be confused with Dinka Bor or with Belanda Viri (Bviri, Ubangian), the contact language mentioned by Storch 2007/Gilley 2004.

tone_statements.quote: Tone is how High or Low the sound of the syllable is, or how the sound rises or falls. ... The word wara ‘shoe’ has Mid, Mid tone and wàrà ‘cotton’ has Low, Low tone. However, these are just two of nine different tone patterns that words can have. Nine different patterns are listed below for words with different syllable patterns. ... High, High waya aunt ... Mid, Mid wara shoe ... Low, Low wàrà cotton, thread ... Mid, High fodo field ... Mid, Low koro year ... High, Low wɔlɔ cough ... High, Mid kuyo sand ... Low, High bɔmɔ mistress ... Low, Mid tofo shadow ... Tone rule: ... If two words with vowel a sound the same except for tone, á is for High tone and à is for Low tone in those words.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory 'Belanda Boor (GM 1434)' (Green & Moran), source Gilley 2004; Grambank bela1256 (source von Heyking 2013); Wikipedia 'Belanda Bor language'
sources.note: PHOIBLE lists three tone levels (high, mid, low) among 38 segments; Grambank codes no prosody; Wikipedia (from von Heyking 2013 via Stirtz 2014) says tone is reduced and non-grammatical; none mentions stress.

sources.citation: Storch, Anne. 2007. Grammatical change and emblematic features in Western Nilotic. In Doris L. Payne & Jaime Peña (eds.), Selected Proceedings of the 37th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 1-15. Somerville, MA: Cascadilla Proceedings Project.
sources.note: Section 4.2 (pp. 9-10) on Belanda Bor covers contact history and prefixal number marking (ka- plural, nyi- singulative) with tone-marked examples; nothing on stress or accent for Belanda Bor (the abbreviation list's stress mark is used for other languages' examples).

sources.citation: Gilley, Leoma G. 2004. The Lwoian family. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 165-174. Khartoum: SIL-Sudan.
sources.note: Family-level orthography survey. On Belanda Boor: unusual consonant system (prenasalized and double plosives from Bviri contact, p. 166), ~9 vowels (p. 169), prefixing number marking (p. 170). Tone: 'All the Lwoian languages included here have three level tones and at least some have contour tones on short vowels' (p. 169). Stress is discussed only for Shilluk (pp. 171-172); nothing on Belanda Boor stress.
